todo_line: - [ ] 006A Implement the approved domain/application scenario “Bob sees Alice join without reloading” against Bob’s already-open club member LiveView, using the committed membership projection notification path and keeping the scenario green.

validation.evidence: 5 tests passed with 0 failures; domain feature discovery, tag filtering and shared acceptance-feature configuration compile with the new step module.
57 tests passed with 0 failures, preserving the accepted dashboard LiveView and committed membership-invalidation behavior.
All Elixir source and test files are formatted.

notes: The only implementation path is web/test/features/step_definitions/live_club_member_list_steps.exs, whose Memba.Cucumber.LiveClubMemberListSteps owns the three formerly undefined exact steps. The five scenario steps have one definition each: the Bob-membership Given reuses Memba.Cucumber.AuthenticationSteps, the viewing step uses LiveClubMemberListSteps, the Alice-not-a-member Given reuses Memba.Cucumber.ClubMemberInvitationSteps, and the When/Then use LiveClubMemberListSteps; repository pattern inspection found no duplicate definition. The viewing step reads the scenario club and Bob records, derives the host from ClubSite.url/1, builds a connection for MembaWeb.Endpoint, installs Bob’s normalized email under IdentityAuth.identity_session_key/0, opens connected /members once, stores that LiveView in context, proves Bob’s stable row is present and proves no Alice member row is initially rendered. After the reused Alice Given supplies her person ID, the When step additionally refutes #club-member-<Alice person_id> against that same open view, generates a fresh membership ID, and calls Memba.Membership.add_member/2 with consistency: :strong; it inserts no projection and sends no ReadModelChanges message itself. The AddClubMember command reaches Memba.Membership.Projectors.Membership, whose after_update/3 publishes the committed notification; the existing Memba source emits the matching {:club_members, club_id} collection invalidation already held by the dashboard query, so a previously absent Alice row can enter. The Then step uses the exact LiveView retained in context and asserts Alice’s stable row selector plus rendered name, with no second live/2, request, patch, reload or navigation. The worker did not edit the selected feature wording/tags or todo.md and introduced no application, package, Docker, release or unrelated migration work. The selected @wip scenario was deliberately not worker-run because the trusted after-worker stage owns that observation; superseded local diagnostics were limited to correcting the formatter target and the required LiveViewTest macro imports/module endpoint before the successful validations recorded above.
